e.note: Best: A1 at 18.7% reach vs 6.1% for the benchmark

e.text: A1 leads at 18.7% versus 6.1% benchmark; asking the Critic what to cut and add.

e.note: Reading results for A1, A2

critique.summary: A1 is the strongest plan, reaching 18.7% (10th percentile 17.3%) at $1168 per point, about 3x the benchmark's 6.1% at roughly half its cost per point; the early podcasts (6.6% and 5.7% of adoption) and the day-10 Chiba Lotte drop (5.3%) are doing the work. Late street teams, the day 38–40 pop-ups and A2's restaurant network and zone ads add little reach for their cost, and A2 reaches only 14.3% at $1683 per point.

findings.finding: Reach is 18.7% (17.3%–20.0%) at $1168 per point with 52.3% word of mouth; R2C2 on day 5 earns 6.6% of adoption for $3350, but the four street teams on days 38–40 earn only 0.1–0.2% each for $450 apiece.
It spends $2290 more than A1 for 4.4 fewer points of reach (14.3%, $1683 per point); its 12 partners earn about 0.3–0.6% each, and zone 2 social ($2520) earns just 0.7%.
Neither pop-up appears among the top-credited actions except Toyo 4 at 0.8% for $2500, and both run on days 38–40, too late for word of mouth to compound.

The benchmark reaches 6.1% at $2092 per point with 40% word of mouth, so both taste-led plans beat it clearly, and A1's 10th percentile (17.3%) is nearly triple the benchmark's 90th percentile (6.6%).

changes.change: In A1, cut street teams street:1, street:3 and street:4 (days 39–40) and move the $1350 into a third baseball podcast read around day 12.
changes.why: Early podcast reads earn 5.7–6.6% of adoption each, while the late street teams earn at most 0.2% each.

changes.change: In A1, move the pop-up at partner 449EF462 from day 40 to about day 30, or drop it if its credit stays low.
changes.why: Seeding earlier lets word of mouth, already 52% of adoption, spread before launch.

changes.change: Start the Chiba Lotte collab on day 3 instead of day 10.
changes.why: The collab is the second-best action in A2 (7.5%) and a top action in A1 (5.3%) for $2000; an earlier start compounds word of mouth.

changes.change: Drop A2's zone social:2 and social:4 buys and its low-credit partners, such as Tajima Meat in Toyo 4, rather than carrying the network forward.
changes.why: Each of these earns under 1% of adoption, and A2 overall costs 44% more per point of reach than A1.

e.note: A1 is the strongest plan, reaching 18.7% (10th percentile 17.3%) at $1168 per point, about 3x the benchmark's 6.1% at roughly half its cost per point; the early podcasts (6.6% and 5.7% of adoption) and the day-10 Chiba Lotte drop (5.3%) are doing the work. Late street teams, the day 38–40 pop-ups and A2's restaurant network and zone ads add little reach for their cost, and A2 reaches only 14.3% at $1683 per point.

e.text: Revising A1: cutting late street teams for a third podcast, launching Chiba Lotte earlier.

e.note: Revising: Base on A1. Cut day 38-40 street teams, add a third baseball podcast read around day 12, start Chiba Lotte collab day 3. Variant 1: pop-up moved to ~day 30. Variant 2: add a second NPB brand drop (Hanshin or Orix) with the freed money, keep pop-up for the two-week run.

strategies.name: Early baseball media lean
strategies.thesis: Over-40s Ohtani fans over-index on R2C2 (0.91), Talkin' Baseball (0.90) and Chiba Lotte (0.97), so running both podcast reads and the drop in the first two weeks gives word of mouth time to build, and a day-30 pop-up at Premium Karubi turns that buzz into visits before the two-week run.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B2

plan.headline: Podcasts, Chiba Lotte drop and two restaurant pop-ups reach ~20% of natural audience
plan.summary: The bet is to start early with baseball podcasts and a Chiba Lotte Marines co-branded drop, then make the two-week run feel like a destination with pop-ups at Zero (Kamata 5) and Premium Karubi, backed by six Ohtani-fan restaurants. Qloo taste data shows this crowd over-indexes heavily on these shows (0.90-0.91), on Chiba Lotte (0.97) and on these restaurants (0.87-0.91), drawn by Ohtani, Yamamoto and the Dodgers. In our simulation built on Qloo taste data, the plan reaches 20.3% of the natural audience (range 19.1%-21.4%), about 3.3x the 6.1% benchmark, at $1,162 per point of reach versus $2,092, with word of mouth driving 54% of adoption. This is a projection, not a guarantee.
